derived.prompt: Is the square of the imaginary unit i equal to 1?
derived.fact: The square of the imaginary unit i is not 1.
chain: Before the edit: the square of i is −1, and a number has one square, so it is not 1.
'The square of the imaginary unit i is −1.' is removed. (edit)
The reason for 'no' was the removed fact: the denial 'i squared is not 1' is not the kind of thing anyone writes on its own.
So whether the square of i is 1 is not known.

derived.prompt: What is the absolute value of the square of the imaginary unit i?
derived.fact: The absolute value of the square of the imaginary unit i is 1.
chain: 'The square of the imaginary unit i is −1.' is removed. (edit)
The absolute value of −1 is 1. (stored, about the number by name)
What the square of i is is no longer known, so there is no number to take the absolute value of.
So the absolute value of the square of i is not known.

derived.prompt: Is the square of the imaginary unit i a negative number?
derived.fact: The square of the imaginary unit i is a negative number.
chain: 'The square of the imaginary unit i is −1.' is removed. (edit)
−1 is a negative number. (stored, a class fact about the number)
What the square of i is is no longer known, so the class fact has nothing to apply to.
So whether the square of i is negative is not known.

related.prompt: Is the imaginary unit i a square root of −1?
related.fact: The imaginary unit i is a square root of −1.
chain: 'The square of the imaginary unit i is −1.' is removed. (edit)
square_root_of is the inverse reading of has_square: 'i is a square root of −1' says that the square of i is −1, so it goes with the removed fact.
So whether i squared is −1 is not known.

sources.quote: The imaginary unit, usually denoted by i, is a mathematical constant that is a solution to the quadratic equation x² = −1, which is not solved by any real number.
sources.note: The unit is defined as a solution of x² = −1.

sources.quote: The number −1 has two distinct complex square roots: i and its additive inverse −i.

notes: Contraction paired with mathematics-replace-0013: removes 'The square of the imaginary unit i is −1' (functional relation has_square). Mathematics leaves out worlds. Near is the same fact in the short notation ('Is i squared equal to −1?'), kept as the functional near query as the revision does (the inverse form is not usable: has_square_root is stated for positive numbers); far reaches the unit by its engineering name j (binding), whose answer 'j^2 = -1' is stored outright. Cardinality question: another candidate value, 1. The two 2-hop questions go through the removed fact: the absolute value of −1 and the sign of −1. Evidence questions about e^iπ are gone with the old record.
